statement: Claims made by the organisations themselves (official websites, archived copies of official websites, SEC filings, their own peer-reviewed papers). None was reproduced by VNX-DNA. They are not comparable with VNX-DNA's SIMULATED numbers and are never put in the same column. Secondary press was used only to find official sources.

claims.claim: "DNA holds one million times more data per unit volume than physical data storage" (general statement about DNA, with Science/Nature/Columbia cited on the page; no Biomemory product figure)
claims.label: company claim, not reproduced

claims.claim: Molecular IT "lasts for centuries" (no measured lifetime given)
claims.label: company claim, not reproduced

claims.claim: March 2026: acquired key assets from Catalog; IP portfolio "more than 90 patents"; production and R&D in Boston
claims.label: company claim, not reproduced

claims.claim: 2024: raised EUR 18 million; June 2026: partnership with Scality
claims.label: company claim, not reproduced

claims.claim: Archived Catalog homepage (May 2025): qualitative claims only (DNA computing, "ultra-dense, stable"); no figures
claims.label: company claim, not reproduced
claims.note: Figures often attributed to Catalog (16 GB English Wikipedia, Shannon writer speeds) were found only in secondary press, not on an official page retrievable today; not tabulated

claims.claim: Atlas Eon 100 (2 Dec 2025): "world's first scalable DNA-based data storage service", "1,000 times denser than magnetic tape", "designed to last for centuries"; no capacity, price, codec or read method stated on the page
claims.label: company claim, not reproduced

claims.claim: "A petabyte-scale archive fits in a 7mm x 18mm capsule"; "synthesizing billions of unique strands simultaneously"
claims.label: company claim, not reproduced

claims.claim: Thalia CMOS DNA synthesis chip: "5.6 billion electro-chemical synthesis sites", "700x increase in synthesis scale over previously available chips" (22 Sep 2026)
claims.label: company claim, not reproduced

claims.claim: Archived homepage (4 Mar 2025): molecular technology "remaining stable and secure for thousands of years"; "Data of Things" (text, image, audio, video embedded in product materials)
claims.label: company claim, not reproduced

claims.claim: Current homepage (accessed 2026-10-11) describes freight/product authentication (SecureShip, Molecular Secure Seal) and makes no DNA data storage claim
claims.label: company claim, not reproduced

claims.claim: Archived homepage (20 May 2024): "programmable DNA data storage material" applied as a coating or integrated into materials; "No centralized network or cloud needed to read back the data"; no figures
claims.label: company claim, not reproduced
claims.note: helix.works returned HTTP 404 and helixworks.com an empty page on 2026-10-11

claims.claim: DNA "extremely dense (up to about 1 exabyte per cubic millimeter)", "durable (half-life of over 500 years)" (general properties of DNA stated on the project page)
claims.label: company claim, not reproduced

claims.claim: 35 files, over 200 MB, in more than 13 million oligonucleotides; each file recovered individually with no errors using random access (Organick et al., Nat. Biotechnol. 2018)
claims.label: published result (peer-reviewed), not reproduced

claims.claim: Automated end-to-end write, store and read of 5 bytes with a custom synthesizer and nanopore sequencing (Takahashi et al., Sci. Rep. 2019)
claims.label: published result (peer-reviewed), not reproduced

claims.claim: "our first DNA data storage solution would be a Century Archive, storing data for 100 years"; expected to be Twist's first commercial DNA data storage solution (Q1 FY2022 results, 4 Feb 2022)
claims.label: company claim, not reproduced
claims.note: Twist moved its storage business into Atlas Data Storage in May 2025 (secondary sources); no current official Century Archive page was found

claims.claim: Official homepage (accessed 2026-10-11): benchtop enzymatic oligo synthesis "overnight"; no DNA data storage claim
claims.label: company claim, not reproduced

claims.claim: Official homepage (accessed 2026-10-11): enzymatic synthesis "up to 900 bp" direct, constructs "up to 50 kb", "sequence-perfect guarantee"; no DNA data storage claim
claims.label: company claim, not reproduced
claims.note: synthesis claims for biology products, not storage oligo pools

claims.claim: 83 kB in 4,991 segments of 158 nt encapsulated in silica, recovered error-free after accelerated ageing; archival for millennia inferred from decay kinetics (Grass et al., Angew. Chem. 2015)
claims.label: published result (peer-reviewed), not reproduced

claims.claim: 'DNA-of-things': 45 kB blueprint in a 3D-printed object over five generations; 1.4 MB video in plexiglass lenses (Koch et al., Nat. Biotechnol. 2020)
claims.label: published result (peer-reviewed), not reproduced

claims.claim: Six codecs benchmarked in silico and in vitro; codecs tolerate error rates up to 14 % and sequence loss of 65 % in isolation; 117 EB/g feasible, 43 EB/g and 13 EB/g demonstrated (Gimpel et al., Nat. Commun. 2026)
claims.label: published result (peer-reviewed), not reproduced
claims.note: the protocol whose harness this lab uses; its published protocol was not re-run here

claims.claim: Motif Caller: ML model detecting whole motifs from raw nanopore signal for motif-based DNA storage; abstract states improved accuracy, no single headline figure (Sci. Rep. 2025)
claims.label: published result (peer-reviewed), not reproduced

no_official_source_found: Helixworks: no figure on any official page retrievable on 2026-10-11 (DNADrive capacity figures exist only in press)
Catalog: Wikipedia/Shannon figures only in secondary press
Iridia: moon-archive press release (GlobeNewswire, 4 Mar 2025) returned HTTP 403; not read, not tabulated
Atlas Eon 100 press release (PR Newswire, 2 Dec 2025): not retrieved; capacity figures quoted by press (e.g. 60 PB in 60 cubic inches) are not tabulated
